claims.text: Severe cryo-rolling followed by warm-rolling will refine the dual-phase lamellar microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1-type eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The hybrid rolling route will produce a heterogeneous nanostructure.
The heterogeneous nanostructure will simultaneously increase room-temperature strength and tensile ductility.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a dual-phase nano-lamellar microstructure containing soft L12/FCC and hard B2 phases.
The initial lamellar colonies possess extensive internal boundaries.
Severe cryo-rolling stores substantial deformation energy.
Warm-rolling after cryo-rolling promotes controlled dynamic recrystallization.
The processed structure will contain ultrafine recrystallized regions together with coarser recovered regions.
The heterogeneous structure will remain a lamellar colony rather than including substantial non-lamellar regions.
Ultrafine recrystallized and coarser recovered regions impede crack initiation and propagation.
Cryo-rolling refines the microstructure in addition to increasing stored energy.
Warm-rolling exploits cryo-rolling-induced stored energy to accelerate recrystallization without coarsening.
Crack deflection and intrinsic toughening at phase boundaries increase tensile ductility.
Hybrid-rolled specimens will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than conventionally processed specimens.
Hybrid-rolled specimens will have greater room-temperature elongation to failure than conventionally processed specimens.
Conventional casting and simple thermo-mechanical processing produce lamellar colonies with limited tensile ductility and lower strength.
The proposed benefits apply to dual-phase lamellar eutectic high-entropy alloys similar to AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The benefits may not transfer to single-phase high-entropy alloys or alloys with substantially different microstructures.

contradictions.description: The mediator describes the product primarily as a heterogeneous nanostructured lamellar colony, whereas the cited evidence reports a heterogeneous mixture of retained lamellar and coarse non-lamellar regions.
